Title: Can I put Infernal Pact on Vidal Jarbeaux ?

Messages.Author: Dr.Mafrune
Messages.Body:
Infernal Pact
Type: Master
Requires: Tremere antitribu
Cost: 1 pool
Unique master.
Put this card on a Tremere antitribu you control and choose a Discipline. The vampire with this card can play cards that require that Discipline as though he or she has the superior version of that Discipline.

Vidal Jarbeaux
Clan: Toreador (group 5)
Capacity: 8
Disciplines: PRE aus cel obf pot
Camarilla: Vidal can meet the clan, sect, or non-infernal vampire trait (e.g., anarch) requirement to play any card. He can meet a given requirement only once each game. +1 bleed.

I don´t know if playing Infernal Pact as Tremere antitribu and choosing a Tremere antitribu count as two different things for Vidals special or only as one.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Dr.Mafrune wrote:
> I don´t know if playing Infernal Pact as Tremere antitribu and choosing a Tremere antitribu count as two different things for Vidals special or only as one.
>
Only as one. When and while playing the card, he emulates the Tremere antitribu clan, because playing the card is an unitary thing.

EDIT: Vidal's special doesn't allow YOU to play Infernal Pact though. But he could play Concert Tour (see my answer below).

Prince of Paris, France

Messages.Author: Sérgio
Messages.Body:
The way I see it: Vidal cannot have the Pact played on him because he can only meet the requirements if he plays a card. Since a master is played by the Methuselah on Vidal, he cannot meet the requirements.

If he could get the Infernal Pact, then he would be able to use the discipline because the Pact allows him to do so, not his ability.

With Mata Hari in play, you can only play the Pact on her, because she is the only one that meets the requirements for the Pact (ergo, you can play Infernal Pact, because you control a vampire that meets the clan requirements, but you can only play it on her).

I think I got it all right, but we could use a O-ruling from Floppy.

Messages.Author: Malcolm Sprye
Messages.Body:
> Squidalot wrote:
> Sure but without a subject for 'to play' you either stick with common English meaning (which for instance in other games would have Vidal meeting the requirements for a player to do something), stick with LSJS view (which is the same) or re-write the ruling which would actually require a rewrite and downgrading of Vidal.
>
To be picky Hugh, what was confusing people is that in the common English, a verb without a subject defaults to the last subject. So the sentence, expanded in common English would be: "Vidal can meet the clan, sect, or non-infernal vampire trait (e.g., anarch) requirement for him to play any card."

I don't think we could generalize this to other games... as many other games don't have cards playing other cards. In V:tES you do, so the expansion above would be valid.

That said, I think (both logically, and based on the posts from LSJ), that indeed he can play masters.

It is likely that I add a few words to Vidal's text to make this clearer.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
Why do I have this habit of delving into rules questions first thing after waking up... uugh

> Camarilla: Vidal can meet the clan, sect, or non-infernal vampire trait (e.g., {Black Hand}) requirement to play any card. He can meet a given requirement only once each game. +1 bleed.
>
> Independent. Red List: Mata Hari has 2 votes (titled). You and she may play cards that require a sect and/or clan as if she were of that required sect and/or clan.
> Artist: Steve Prescott
>
The reason why Vidal and Mata Hari are different, is that Mata Hari specifically mentions the player in the card text. Mata Hari allows the player to play Ventrue HQ as if Mata Hari was a ventrue (she fulfills the requirement of a ventrue in play).

Vidal doesn't refer to the player. He refers only to himself. "To play any card" refers to Vidal playing the card. Therefore he shouldn't fulfill the requirements of playing master cards.

However, you apparently have LSJ ruling from the paleolithic period saying otherwise. So I see three options:
1. Errata Vidals cardtext to mention the player "for you and Vidal to play any card", mirroring Mata Haris text.
2. Obey the existing card text and actually rule against LSJ for once
3. Ban Vidal (I would shed no tears if you choose this option)

ps. We can all be silently thankful to BCP for omitting Vidal's reprint among the recent Keepers of the Tradition reprints.
